data.why: A gas range (cuisinière) in a room: the story starts with a pot on an open flame on a stone hearth, then builds the range around it one real part at a time (steel walls and a grate, a valve and a knob, then an oven door, lid and hood). The camera opens close on the pot and flame, stays mid on the range for the problems and fixes, and ends on the home view with the flame working calmly.

ideas.idea: set a pot over an open fire and you already have the idea of a stove
the open flame throws heat all over the room, and cooking is the top cause of home fires
box the fire in with steel walls and put the pot on a grate
the trapped heat is all or nothing, so the soup boils over and runs down the front
add a gas valve and a knob that turns the flame down
this box with a burner, a valve and a knob is a gas range
gas flows through the valve to the burner, and a rotten-egg smell is added so you notice leaks
the blue flame burns at about 1950 degrees, so the knob matters
the gas stove is not a French invention, whatever the French word cuisinière suggests
it was an Englishman, James Sharp, who patented it in 1826
an oven door, a pot lid and a hood with a light complete the range
calm end: the range stands finished with its flame burning under the lid
